text: LaLonde compares nonexperimental training earnings estimates against an experimental benchmark and reports substantial specification problems.
Dehejia and Wahba obtain closer experimental-benchmark estimates using propensity scores, with causal interpretation relying on selection on observables and overlap.
Imbens and Xu emphasize that stable adjusted differences from modern methods do not by themselves establish causal interpretation.
Lakens distinguishes nonsignificance from evidence of practical equivalence and recommends prespecified meaningful equivalence bounds.
Propensity-score adjustment addresses observed covariates under ignorability; balancing observed covariates does not itself establish absence of unobserved confounding.
Chernozhukov and coauthors give an orthogonal ATTE score, cross-fitting algorithm and asymptotic score-based inference under overlap, moment and nuisance-rate conditions.
Crump and coauthors show that limited overlap can impair precision and increase specification sensitivity; restricting to better-overlap populations changes the target population.
Holm provides a sequentially rejective multiple-testing procedure protecting against rejection of any true null in the family.
LaLonde explicitly reports historical earnings in 1982 dollars; those units cannot be assigned to a synthetic cohort merely from similarly named earnings variables.
